title: MDH Zoonoses: IP-1 Exposed Workers — Tracker v1

fields.fromName: Ingrid Solberg, MPH (MDH Zoonotic Diseases Unit)
fields.subject: CONFIDENTIAL — HEALTH: IP-1 exposed workers — tracker v1
fields.body:
Director Naomi Eshleman,

The reconciled list has 37 people who entered the IP-1 barns since 10/14: 9 farm and load-out staff, 11 from Catch Crew C, and 17 others (maintenance, vet, dead haul, feed). Depop crew members who go into the barns today still need to be added.

Status: 14 reached and counseled, 5 started on oseltamivir.

Not reached: 8 of the 11 Crew C workers. On the cooperative's list, 3 Crew C phone numbers are disconnected, and 2 workers are listed by first name only, with no number. Four Crew C members speak K'iche' as their first language. After a call in Spanish, the crew lead told us they "understood," but none of the crew has picked up medication.

A separate issue: Prairie Gold HR emailed us asking for "a list of which workers are on Tamiflu so we can schedule shifts." We have not replied.

How do you want to handle both?

Ingrid
fields.signature:
Ingrid Solberg, MPH
Epidemiologist, Zoonotic Diseases Unit
Minnesota Department of Health
555-0164 | ingrid.solberg@mdh-zoonoses.example
CONFIDENTIAL: contains protected health information. Do not forward.

instructorNote: This inject tests whether Public Health counts a worker as reached only when that worker understands the message. Look for a K'iche' interpreter, in person or by phone, and work with the crew lead to find the 2 workers listed by first name only. Public Health should start 10-day monitoring from each person's last exposure, restarting the clock for anyone who goes back into the barns. Public Health should turn down Prairie Gold HR's request and share health data only with MDH.
